text:
alex-pm: Quick sync — we need to decide whether the chat completions API should treat a single `prompt` string and `messages[]` as equally first-class or force a single canonical shape. Customer asks: some legacy apps still send `prompt`, others already use `messages`.
sara-eng: My inclination is canonicalize on `messages[]` (role + content). It's cleaner for streaming, tools, and partial decoding. Backwards compat for `prompt` is doable as a translation layer.

mike-sdk: +1 for messages. SDK ergonomics matter though. If we accept `prompt` we should auto-convert to `messages:[{role: \"user\", content: prompt}]` in the client to avoid two divergent code paths.

lina-design: From UX side: docs and examples confuse users if both shapes are equally promoted. Prefer single canonical example with a small section \"legacy `prompt`\" that shows migration.

alex-pm: Important constraints: launch criteria must include clear migration path, no behavioral regressions for existing customers, and small surface area for monitoring. Also need to surface role semantics (system/user/assistant) clearly.

tom-cs: We have one paying customer with heavy prompt-rewrite pipelines that rely on the plain string. They want zero-change server-side for now. Can we offer a compatibility header or opt-in translation mode?

sara-eng: Implementing server-side translation flag is straightforward: `X-Redwood-Prompt-compat: true`. If present, API will accept `prompt` and map it to `messages` before routing to runtime. Default off for new apps.

mike-sdk: Could default our official SDKs to send `messages` (recommended) and include a `compat: true` option to mimic legacy behavior. That keeps server complexity minimal.

alex-pm: OK. Proposal: canonical shape = `messages[]`. Compatibility: accept `prompt` when `X-Redwood-Prompt-Compat: true` OR when request comes from legacy API key list for 12 months. Launch blocker?

lina-design: Docs + migration guide should be ready before GA. Include quick copy samples for Python/JS and a small interactive tool.

sara-eng: Engineering asks: define exact mapping rules for special cases — e.g., if `prompt` contains multiple messages separated by `\n\n### Assistant:` style markers, do we attempt to parse or leave as single user message? My vote: no heuristic parsing — treat as single user message.

mike-sdk: Agreed. Simpler and deterministic. If customers want parsing they should pre-format into `messages`.

alex-pm: Also need to decide system role enforcement. Current chaos: some clients embed system instructions as first user messages. We should allow explicit `role: \"system\"` but add a soft validation warning if system content is included not in `role: system`.

tom-cs: That warning must be non-breaking for existing customers. Send via diagnostic header `Redwood-Warn: system-role-mismatch` and include suggestion text in dev console.

alex-pm: For rollout plan: (1) beta scoped to customers who opt-in, (2) collect compatibility metrics (errors, warnings, latency), (3) GA after 8 weeks or earlier if no major regressions. Acceptance criteria: no >0.5% increase in error-rate on migrated traffic, latency within 5% of baseline, docs + SDKs published.

sara-eng: Engineering tasks: server-side translation implementation, validation warnings, header parsing, telemetry events `compat_prompt_used` and `system_role_mismatch`. Estimate: 2 sprints.

mike-sdk: SDK tasks: default to `messages[]` examples, add `compat` flag, and helper `migrate_prompt_to_messages(prompt)` snippet. 1 sprint + docs.

lina-design: Design tasks: examples, migration micro-site, and a one-page checklist for Solutions Engineers. 1 sprint.

alex-pm: Edge-case decisions: 1) structured outputs and tools — these require `messages` for tool-calling contract, do not support `prompt`-only flows for tool invocation. 2) function-calling metadata only with `messages` role tagging. Call these non-negotiable.

sara-eng: Agree. We'll return 400 if request uses `prompt` and also requests tool/function calling unless compat header present and translation succeeded.

mike-sdk: Can we add an ephemeral migration mode that logs sample payload translations for customers so they can validate? Helpful for big clients.

tom-cs: Yes please — we'll use that for the big customer. Name it `X-Redwood-Dry-Translate: true` and return `translated_messages` in a non-production debug field in the response.

alex-pm: Final asks for this thread: Sara, create an engineering RFC with API details and sample JSON mappings. Mike, add SDK prototype that performs auto-convert with `compat` opt-in. Lina, draft migration copy. Tom, get customer sign-off on compatibility header approach. I'll own rollout timing and acceptance metrics.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline note: feature flags ready in staging, rollout gate for beta will be `flag:chat_prompt_compat`. Use `canary-percent` rollout if opted-in customers are >1% of traffic.

alex-pm: Thanks everyone — let's sync in next PLM. :thumbsup:
